q: In buildings of 10 storeys and higher, how often is a yoke vent required?
o: Every 3 to 5 floors
Every floor
Every 10 floors
Only at the top floor
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 9 / Ch. 2 definitions
n: The yoke vent ties the soil stack to the vent stack so pressure swings in a tall stack are relieved along its height.

q: What is a loop vent?
o: A vent that serves a single trap only
A group vent looping back to the stack vent
A vent that also carries waste water
A vent linking two stacks at every floor
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 9 / Ch. 2 definitions
n: A loop vent is like a circuit vent, but it loops back to the stack vent instead of the vent stack. It is used on the top floor.

q: What does a relief vent do?
o: Carries waste from a fixture to the stack
Removes odors from a toilet room
Lets air move between the drainage and vent systems
Drains condensate from the vent stack
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 9 / Ch. 2 definitions
n: Relief vents let air in or out where pressure builds, as in long horizontal drains or tall stacks.

q: What is vent piping sized from?
o: The height of the building only
The floor area of the building
The roof area drained
Fixture units served and developed length
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 9 / Ch. 2 definitions
n: Code tables give the vent size for the fixture units connected and the developed length.

q: How far above the roof must a vent extend?
o: At least 0.15 m
At least 0.05 m
At least 1.0 m
At least 2.1 m
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 9 / Ch. 2 definitions
n: Vent terminals: at least 0.15 m above the roof, 0.30 m from any vertical surface, and 0.90 m above or 3.0 m away from any openable window or door.

q: How are vent pipes finished where they pass through the roof?
o: With an open gap around it for air
Watertight, with approved flashing
With a screw cap closing the top
Painted, with no flashing at all
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 9 / Ch. 2 definitions
n: Rain must not leak in around the pipe.

q: What is a circuit vent?
o: A vent that serves one trap only
A vent that also carries waste water
A group vent from a branch to the vent stack
A vent that runs through the roof alone
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 9 / Ch. 2 definitions
n: One circuit vent serves a battery of fixtures on a horizontal branch.

q: What is a wet vent?
o: A vent that carries only air
A vent that drains rainwater from the roof
A vent flooded by a blocked stack
A vent that also carries waste water
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 9 / Ch. 2 definitions
n: Part of a drain can vent other fixtures as long as it is sized large enough to carry both.

q: When may the horizontal part of a vent exceed one-third of its total length?
o: When the whole vent is one size larger
Never, under any conditions
When it is made of cast iron
When it runs above a ceiling
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 9 / Ch. 2 definitions
n: Long horizontal vents create more friction, so the larger size makes up for it.

q: When may two fixtures share one vertical vent?
o: Never; each fixture needs its own vent
When they connect at the same level, as a common vent
Only if they are water closets
Only if they are on different floors
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 9 / Ch. 2 definitions
n: A common (unit, dual) vent serves two traps set back to back or side by side at one level.

q: For a vent terminal on a roof deck used by people, how high above the deck must it rise?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 9 / Ch. 2 definitions
n: Where people use the roof, vent terminals rise 2.1 m or sit at least 3.0 m away horizontally.

q: What is a group vent?
o: A vent that serves one trap
A vent that carries waste
A vent for a single floor drain
A vent that serves two or more traps
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 9 / Ch. 2 definitions
n: Circuit, loop and common vents are all group vents.

q: What is a dry vent?
o: A vent that carries no liquid waste
A vent that also carries waste water
A vent that drains condensate
A vent without a roof extension
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 9 / Ch. 2 definitions
n: Most vents are dry vents; wet vents are the exception.

q: How are changes in direction made in vent piping?
o: By heating and bending the pipe
With approved fittings, never by bending the pipe
With any fitting, even drainage-prohibited ones
By cutting the pipe at an angle and taping it
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 9 / Ch. 2 definitions
n: Bent or strained pipe cracks and leaks sewer gas.

q: Where must a vent opening be in relation to the trap weir?
o: Below the trap weir
At the bottom of the trap
Not below the trap weir
Anywhere along the drain
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 9 / Ch. 2 definitions
n: A vent below the weir fills with waste and siphons the trap.

q: For a vent terminal near a roof deck used by people, how far away horizontally must it be?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 9 / Ch. 2 definitions
n: Either 3.0 m away or 2.1 m high keeps sewer gas from people using the deck.

q: What is a branch vent?
o: A horizontal vent joining fixture vents to a stack
The main vertical vent of the building
A vent that also carries waste water
The part of a stack above its highest drain
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 9 / Ch. 2 definitions
n: Branch vents gather individual vents on a floor.

q: What is a common (unit, dual) vent?
o: A vent serving a whole floor
A vent serving two traps at the same level
A vent that also carries waste
The vent at the top of a stack
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 9 / Ch. 2 definitions
n: Back-to-back lavatories often share one common vent.

q: May galvanized steel or wrought iron vent pipe be laid underground?
o: Yes, if it is painted first
Yes, if the soil is dry
No; keep it at least 152 mm above ground
Yes, if it is wrapped in tape
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 9 / Ch. 2 definitions
n: Galvanizing corrodes quickly in soil.

q: How is a vent sized where it passes through the roof?
o: One pipe size smaller
Kept at 32 mm, always
The same size as below
One pipe size larger (VSTR)
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 9 / Ch. 2 definitions
n: The bigger size keeps the opening from closing with frost, debris or spider webs.

q: How far must a vent extend above a roof or fire wall it passes through?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 9 / Ch. 2 definitions
n: Vent terminals: at least 0.15 m above the roof, 0.30 m from any vertical surface, and 0.90 m above or 3.0 m away from any openable window or door.

q: What is an individual vent (revent)?
o: A vent serving two or more traps
A vent for one trap, joining higher up
A vent that also carries waste
The main vent of the building
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 9 / Ch. 2 definitions
n: Individual vents give each trap its own air supply.

q: What is a stack vent?
o: A vertical vent running beside the stack
A horizontal vent connected to the stack
The stack's extension above its highest drain
A vent serving a floor drain
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 9 / Ch. 2 definitions
n: The stack vent carries the top of the stack through the roof. A vent stack is a separate pipe alongside.

q: Which of these is NOT a listed vent pipe material?
o: Cast iron
Copper
PVC-DWV
Vitrified clay
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 9 / Ch. 2 definitions
n: Vents may be cast or ductile iron, galvanized steel or wrought iron, lead, copper, brass, ABS or PVC.

q: How high must a vent be before it turns horizontal?
o: 152 mm above the highest flood-level rim
Right at the level of the trap weir
At the level of the finished floor
Just under the ceiling of the room
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 9 / Ch. 2 definitions
n: If the drain blocks and the fixture fills, the water must not rise into the horizontal vent.

q: How far horizontally must a vent terminal be from any openable window or door?
o: At least 0.30 m
At least 3.0 m
At least 0.90 m
At least 1.5 m
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 9 / Ch. 2 definitions
n: Vent terminals: at least 0.15 m above the roof, 0.30 m from any vertical surface, and 0.90 m above or 3.0 m away from any openable window or door.

q: What minimum size must an individual vent be, compared with the drain it serves?
o: Equal to the drain diameter
At least twice the drain diameter
At least half its diameter, and not under 32 mm
At least 76 mm, always
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 9 / Ch. 2 definitions
n: Half the drain diameter lets enough air in to protect the trap.

q: What is the vent stack?
o: The part of a soil stack above the highest drain
A vent that serves one trap
A vent that also carries waste
The main vertical vent that carries air to and from the drainage system
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 9 / Ch. 2 definitions
n: The vent stack runs alongside the soil stack for its full height.

q: When may a vent be omitted?
o: When an interceptor drains indirectly to a vented receptor
When the fixture is on the ground floor
When the trap is an ordinary P-trap
When the pipe is larger than 102 mm
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 9 / Ch. 2 definitions
n: The indirect connection breaks the siphon, and the receptor has its own trap and vent.

q: How does a vent take off from a horizontal drain?
o: From the bottom of the drain
With its invert above the drain's centerline
From the side, at the drain's invert
Below the drain
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 9 / Ch. 2 definitions
n: Taking off above the centerline keeps waste from running into the vent.

q: How high above an openable window or door must a vent terminal be, if within 3.0 m of it?
o: At least 0.15 m
At least 0.30 m
At least 0.90 m
At least 2.1 m
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 9 / Ch. 2 definitions
n: Vent terminals: at least 0.15 m above the roof, 0.30 m from any vertical surface, and 0.90 m above or 3.0 m away from any openable window or door.

q: What is the minimum diameter of an individual vent?
o: 25 mm (1 in)
51 mm (2 in)
76 mm (3 in)
32 mm (1¼ in)
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 9 / Ch. 2 definitions
n: Smaller vents clog and do not pass enough air.

q: What does a local vent do?
o: Carries foul air from a fixture or room outdoors
Protects a trap seal from siphonage
Carries waste water from a fixture
Relieves pressure in a tall stack
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 9 / Ch. 2 definitions
n: A local vent takes odors away from a fixture. It is not part of the drainage vent system.

q: What is the main purpose of venting a drainage system?
o: To carry rainwater from the roof
To protect trap seals from siphonage
To cool the drainage pipes
To make waste flow faster
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 9 / Ch. 2 definitions
n: Vents let air in and out so the water in each trap stays in place.

q: How must horizontal vent pipes be laid?
o: Perfectly level, with no slope
With drops to collect condensate
Without sags, graded to drain back
Sloping away from the drain
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 9 / Ch. 2 definitions
n: Water left in a sag blocks the air.

q: How far must a vent terminal be from any vertical surface?
o: At least 0.15 m
At least 0.90 m
At least 3.0 m
At least 0.30 m
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 9 / Ch. 2 definitions
n: Vent terminals: at least 0.15 m above the roof, 0.30 m from any vertical surface, and 0.90 m above or 3.0 m away from any openable window or door.
